identificationModule.briefTitle: Cadonilimab(AK104) Plus Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy in Patients With Locally Advanced, Unresectable, Stage III NSCLC
identificationModule.officialTitle: Lung-AK104 Study: Cadonilimab(AK104) Plus Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy in Patients With Locally Advanced, Unresectable, Stage Lll Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer

descriptionModule.briefSummary:
The goal of this single arm, phase II clinical trial is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of cadonilimab (AK104) as induction and consolidation therapy in locally advanced/unresectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients treated with concurrent chemoradiotherapy.

Participants will receive 2 cycles of induction therapy with cadonilimab combined with carboplatin/cisplatin plus etoposide, followed by standard concurrent chemoradiotherapy (thoracic radiotherapy + carboplatin/cisplatin plus etoposide regimen chemotherapy), and finally consolidation therapy with cadonilimab (AK104) for 1 year.

interventions.name: Cadonilimab (AK104)
interventions.description: Participants will receive 2 cycles of induction therapy with cadonilimab combined with carboplatin/cisplatin plus etoposide, followed by standard concurrent chemoradiotherapy (thoracic radiotherapy + carboplatin/cisplatin plus etoposide), and finally consolidation therapy with cadonilimab (AK104) for 1 year.

primaryOutcomes.description: According to RECISIT1.1 criteria, the proportion of patients achieving CR and PR as their best response before initial disease progression was evaluated.

primaryOutcomes.measure: The incidence rate of treatment-related adverse events
primaryOutcomes.description: The proportion of treatment-related toxicity to the total number of evaluable cases was evaluated according to CTCAE 5.0 criteria.

secondaryOutcomes.description: Objective response rate was evaluated according to RECIST 1.1 criteria after two courses of Cadonilimab combined with EP chemotherapy and before the start of concurrent chemoradiotherapy

secondaryOutcomes.measure: disease control rate before Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy
